answer:
ANSWER: 163 genes.

Using DESeq2 (design ~ Media + Strain, Strain reference = JBX1), with Benjamini–Hochberg FDR < 0.05 applied independently to each of the three strain-vs-JBX1 contrasts:
  A = DE in ΔlasI single mutant  (strain 97 vs JBX1)  = 1980
  B = DE in ΔrhlI single mutant  (strain 98 vs JBX1)  = 2298
  C = DE in ΔlasIΔrhlI double mutant (strain 99 vs JBX1) = 3132
  |A ∪ B| = 2553   (|A∩B| = 1725)
  |A ∩ C| = 1880,  |B ∩ C| = 2189
  FINAL  |(A ∪ B) \ C| = 163

So 163 genes are differentially expressed in at least one single mutant but not in the double mutant.

CAVEAT (one sentence): R/DESeq2 was not installed in the execution environment (no R binary anywhere on the filesystem and no internet to install it), so this is a faithful Python DESeq2-equivalent — median-of-ratios size factors, NB GLM with per-gene MLE dispersion shrunk toward a mean-trend, Wald test, and naive per-contrast BH — and the exact R-DESeq2 count may differ modestly (a dispersion-variant sensitivity check gave a robust range of 138–171, centered on 163).

Key assumptions carried through (as agreed): strain 1 = JBX1 (wild type) and strain 99 = ΔlasIΔrhlI (double; supported by largest effect + lowest QS-effector expression); strains 97/98 are the two single mutants (order irrelevant to the union); DESeq2 default filtering (only all-zero genes dropped — here none, so all 5828 retained); naive BH adj.p < 0.05 (not DESeq2 independent filtering).
